approachQuestion.prompt: An immutable token list represents nested lists: a list starts with OPEN and ends with CLOSE, and contains integers or other lists. One outer list is guaranteed, with valid nesting and 2 <= n <= 200,000 tokens. Each integer contributes its value multiplied by its depth: integers directly inside the outer list have depth 1. Return the total. All integers and weighted partial sums fit signed 64-bit integers. Empty lists are legal. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total time. Input: [OPEN,2,OPEN,3,CLOSE,4,CLOSE]. Output: 12, from 2*1+3*2+4*1.

options.text: Scan tokens, increment depth on OPEN and decrement on CLOSE; add integer times current depth to a running total.
options.feedback: The valid input already supplies the nesting order, so only the current depth is needed to weight the next integer.

options.text: Push a depth marker for every OPEN and pop on CLOSE; weight each integer by the number of active markers.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but separate markers store a whole active path when its length alone determines every weight.

options.text: Add all integers without tracking list boundaries.
options.feedback: The example would total 9 rather than 12 because the nested 3 has weight 2.

options.text: Find maximum depth, then multiply the sum of every integer by that maximum.
options.feedback: The example has maximum depth 2, but 2 and 4 belong at depth 1; this method returns 18 instead of 12.

feedback.reason: A stack is unnecessary when all unresolved frames contribute only their count.
details: Start depth and total at zero. OPEN increases depth; CLOSE decreases it. For an integer add its value times depth. The guaranteed valid nesting lets a scalar replace a stack of identical markers.

Guaranteed valid nesting makes every active marker interchangeable for this sum, so depth alone suffices. Multiply each integer by its current nesting depth; counting all integers equally loses their structural weight.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For depth-counter-sum, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: Input is immutable and excluded; output is one excluded scalar. Depth and sums fit one fixed-size word.
No stack, recursion, hashing, copied input or output buffer is used; arithmetic takes constant time.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One depth counter replaces an unnecessary stack of identical scope markers.
details: The scan reads all n tokens with constant arithmetic per token. Only depth and total are retained, so auxiliary space is O(1); input and scalar output are excluded.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The analyzed counter method retains only depth and sum, not a frame for each open list.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Every token is read once; earlier nested lists are never rescanned.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Even a flat list requires reading all integers in the worst case.
